MEMORANDUM

  Agenda Item #: 5
  Meeting Date: January 28, 2020

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

THRU:  KENNETH RUKAVINA, ACTING CITY MANAGER /s/

FROM:  CARL MORITZ, URBAN FORESTER /s/

SUBJECT: CONSIDERATION OF PARKLANDS COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATIONS OF
  JANUARY 9, 2020

DATE:  JANUARY 28, 2020

Issue/Purpose

The purpose of this memorandum is to transmit Parklands Committee recommendation for applications
from the January 9, 2020 meeting to the City Council.

Background/Discussion

At its meeting of January 9, 2020, the Parklands Committee reviewed and discussed six items. The first
item was a citizen application was for removal of the existing street trees and change of the designated
street tree. The second item was a citizen application for tree removal to restore the view. The third item
was a citizen application for street tree removal for safety. The fourth item was a review of the designated
street tree for Cloyden Road. The fifth item was to change the meeting time for the Parklands Committee
and the last item was the ad hoc committee policy recommendations to address parkland encroachments.

1.  PC-524-20; Application to remove 3 London Plane trees and change of the designated street tree
  adjacent to 2825 Via Neve

  Applicant:  Jennifer Alvarez
  2612 Via Rivera
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff indicated the purpose of the application was to remove the existing street trees and replace them
with trees that are not designated. The existing London Plane trees are unpermitted and nonconforming

  1
 trees that are in a deteriorated condition and are encroaching into other residents views. The designated
street tree, the Mediterranean Fan palm, was designated in 2001 but the palm is only planted at one
address of the 12 homes on the street. The public street trees and private neighborhood trees has an
eclectic character with some tall trees encroaching into the views.

The applicant indicated the London Plane trees were poorly adapted to this climate and were in very poor
health. The applicant expressed, if the London Plane trees are to stay, they would encroach into her
neighbor’s views. The applicant felt the Magnolia would enhance the architecture of her Cape Cod design
and would provide more screening from the street without the trees encroaching into her neighbor’s
views.

The Committee agreed the London Plane trees should be removed but were initially split on the re-
designation. One member felt the designated street tree change should be denied if there was not adequate
notice to the residents to change the street tree. After additional discussion concerning the notice the
residents received through the posting, a door to door communication by the applicant, a survey with the
adjacent residents signatures from adjacent properties, and the Committee’s ability to approve a change
of designation adjacent to one home when there is no established neighborhood character, the Committee
agreed with the change of designation adjacent to this one address.

Action: Committee member Leach motioned second by Cooper to recommend to the City Council
approval to remove three London Plane trees located in the parkway adjacent to 2825 Via Neve
according to the ‘Standard Conditions For Tree Removal Approvals’. Require removal of the
stumps and waive the payment to the ‘Tree Bank’ for removal of non-designated trees. Recommend
approval of the change of the designated street tree to the Magnolia grandiflora ‘Little Gem’
adjacent to 2825 Via Neve. The vote was (3-0-1-1, in favor, Groves absent and Richie-Bray
recused).

2.  PC-529-20; Application to remove Jacaranda tree located in the parkway adjacent to 2820 Via
  Pacheco.

  Applicant:  Michele Cohen
  2820 Via Pacheco
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this application as a request for view restoration. The unpermitted and nonconforming
Jacaranda was planted in between two Olive trees, the previously designated street tree, and had been
repetitively topped to keep below the view but is now encroaching into the view and on the Olive trees.

The applicant was concerned with view restoration and expressed dissatisfaction with the trees flowering
characteristic and the mess that followed and also the security of their front door.

The Committee were in agreement concerning the Jacaranda’s view encroachment. They all agreed it
was not the neighborhood character or the designated street tree and should be approved.

Action: Committee member Cooper motioned seconded by McCabe to recommend to the City
Council approval to remove one Jacaranda tree located in the parkway adjacent to 2820 Via
Pacheco according to the ‘Standard Conditions For Tree Removal Approvals’. Require a $500
payment to the ‘Tree Bank’ and removal of the stump. The vote was (3-0-1-1, in favor, Groves
absent and Leach recused).

  2
 3.  PC-530-20; Application to remove one Carob tree located in the parkway adjacent to 2609 Via
  Rivera.

  Applicant:  John Kunich
  2609 Via Rivera
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this application to remove one Carob tree as a request to improve safety when backing
out of their driveway. The Carob tree was the previously designated street tree for Via Rivera but was
changed to a smaller Magnolia Saint Mary in 2001 for view concerns. This tree was also approved to be
removed in 2015 but had not been acted on and the one year approval had expired.

The applicant provided a number of reasons to approve the removal of the tree including two new young
drivers and friends using the driveway, a busy street with two local schools nearby and sap dripping from
the tree on the driveway restricting parking options. The applicant also requested the Committee waive
the payment to the ‘Tree Bank’.

The Committee understood and agreed with the safety concerns but were concerned about deviating from
the normal requirement of payment to the ‘Tree Bank’. Payment to the ‘Tree Bank’ is optional when
nonconforming trees are approved for removal. The first motion requiring payment to the ‘Tree Bank’
failed to receive a second.

Action: Committee member Cooper motioned second by McCabe to recommend approval to the
City Council to remove one Carob tree located in the parkway adjacent to 2609 Via Rivera with
modification. The vote was (3-1-1, in favor, Groves absent and Richie-Bray dissenting).

4.  Consideration of a new designated street tree for Cloyden Road.

Staff introduced this item as a re-designation of the designated street tree for Cloyden Road. A history of
the process and criteria for tree selection were presented. A slide show tour of the street and views was
presented along with a list of 12 trees as suggested options with pictures.

The resident of 740 Cloyden Road spoke and suggested more impute be gathered from the residents on
the street. A second resident on the street defended the existing tall Eucalyptus trees appreciating the
character and view under the trees and advocated more tall trees be designated.

The Committee discussed the list and wanted to reduce the number of options and gather more community
impute. The Committee decided to vote to reduce the list to three and re-post for the next meeting.

Action: Committee member Richie-Bray motioned second by Cooper to recommend reducing the
options to the Crape Myrtle, Strawberry and Weeping Bottlebrush trees and re-notice the street.
The vote was (4-0-1, in favor, Groves absent).

5.  Change of the meeting time for the Parklands Committee.

The Committee requested this be on the agenda and publicly noticed as required. The request was to
move the time to 6:30PM. All member were in agreement to start the meeting consistent with other

  3
 committees/commissions and the earlier start will help for meeting that have a tendency to go late in the
night.

Action: Committee member Cooper motioned second by Richie-Bray to recommend approval to
the City Council to change the start time for the Parklands Committee to 6:30PM starting at the
March meeting. The vote was (4-1, in favor, Groves absent).

A change in start time shall be pursuant to a resolution adopted by the City Council, which will be
agendized as a separate action item.

6.  Encroachments Ad Hoc Committee Report

Staff presented a draft of the Encroachment Abatement policy document to committee members. The
purpose of the report was to provide policy recommendations to present to the City Council.

The discussion among the Committee concerned the fine amounts within the city for other violations, the
difference between the existing policies and the Municipal Code, time frames for compliance, notice to
residents, and evidence of compliance to start the clock.

John Harbison, Christine McNamara, Janine Nendick, and Ried Schott spoke during public comment.

Parklands Committee recommends to City Council to modify policies to address encroachments to be
calendared for City Council’s consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Notification

Interested parties attending the Parklands Committee meeting were made aware that the above noted
recommendations would be transmitted to the City Council. This item is also noticed in the standard
manner for City Council meetings.

Alternatives Available to the City Council

City Council has the option to approve, deny, amend or remand this item to the Parklands Committee.
Should the City Council consider amending and have its own hearing on this item, it is recommended
that the discussion be calendared for a future meeting so appropriate notice can be assured.

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council review and approve the Parklands Committee recommended
actions of January 9, 2020.
